# onetsolutions_instance_ip_reverse_dns (Resource)

Manages the reverse DNS (PTR) hostname of an IPv4 address of an instance.

The hostname must already resolve to the address (an `A` record): this is checked before the
change is accepted. Applying waits until the hostname is in place.

**Destroying this resource only removes it from the state**: a reverse DNS cannot be reset, so the
address keeps its last hostname until it is set again. Once the instance is cancelled or
terminated, the next refresh removes this resource from the state.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# The hostname must already resolve to the address before its reverse DNS is set.
resource "onetsolutions_dns_record" "mail" {
  zone_id = onetsolutions_dns_zone.example.id
  type    = "A"
  name    = "mail"
  content = onetsolutions_instance.mail.primary_ipv4
}

resource "onetsolutions_instance_ip_reverse_dns" "mail" {
  instance_id = onetsolutions_instance.mail.id
  address     = onetsolutions_instance.mail.primary_ipv4
  reverse_dns = "mail.example.com"

  depends_on = [onetsolutions_dns_record.mail]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `instance_id` (String) The UUID of the instance the address is assigned to. Changing it targets another address (replacement).
- `reverse_dns` (String) The fully qualified hostname, such as `mail.example.com`: lowercase, without a trailing dot. It must resolve to the address. Can be changed in place.

### Optional

- `address` (String) The IPv4 address itself, such as `203.0.113.10`, resolved to its UUID among the instance's addresses. Exactly one of `ip_address_id` and `address` is set; the other is computed. Setting a different one targets another address (replacement).
- `ip_address_id` (String) The UUID of the address. Exactly one of `ip_address_id` and `address` is set; the other is computed. Setting a different one targets another address (replacement).
- `organization_id` (String) The organization the object belongs to. Defaults to the provider's `organization_id` when the object is created; changing it explicitly recreates the object.
- `project_id` (String) The project the object belongs to. Defaults to the provider's `project_id` when the object is created; changing it explicitly recreates the object.
- `timeouts` (Block, Optional) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--timeouts))

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The UUID of the IP address.

<a id="nestedblock--timeouts"></a>
### Nested Schema for `timeouts`

Optional:

- `create` (String) How long to wait for the creation, as a duration such as "30s" or "2h45m". Defaults to `10m`.
- `update` (String) How long to wait for the update, as a duration such as "30s" or "2h45m". Defaults to `10m`.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `id` attribute, for example:

```terraform
import {
  to = onetsolutions_instance_ip_reverse_dns.mail
  id = "3f2a9c1e-5b7d-4e8f-9a0b-1c2d3e4f5a6b/8b1d4e2f-6c3a-4f9e-8d7b-2a1c0e9f8d7c/9a0b1c2d-3e4f-4a5b-8c6d-7e8f9a0b1c2d/6e7f8a9b-0c1d-4e2f-9a3b-4c5d6e7f8a9b"
}
```

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# <organization_id>/<project_id>/<instance_id>/<ip_address_id>, or <instance_id>/<ip_address_id> when the provider sets organization_id and project_id.
terraform import onetsolutions_instance_ip_reverse_dns.mail 3f2a9c1e-5b7d-4e8f-9a0b-1c2d3e4f5a6b/8b1d4e2f-6c3a-4f9e-8d7b-2a1c0e9f8d7c/9a0b1c2d-3e4f-4a5b-8c6d-7e8f9a0b1c2d/6e7f8a9b-0c1d-4e2f-9a3b-4c5d6e7f8a9b
```
